paper_records.paper_title: Mechanical response of single and double-helix SMA wire ropes
paper_records.matrix_filename: A3-2022-Mechanical response of single and double-helix.pdf
paper_records.why_added: Highest-threat full-text prior art paper for Target T1 and foundational benchmark for H0b.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Directly closes T1 and demonstrates H0b sufficiency by modeling 3D NiTi multiwire bundles with Coulomb friction and Auricchio superelasticity.
paper_records.method: 3D nonlinear continuum finite element analysis in Abaqus/Standard with custom UMAT
paper_records.material_or_system: 1x27 single-helix and 7x7 double-helix superelastic NiTi wire ropes
paper_records.loading_mode: Quasi-static cyclic uniaxial tension under fixed-end rotation
paper_records.control_variables: Displacement control, isothermal room temperature (22 deg C)
paper_records.independent_variables: Cable architecture (1x27 vs 7x7), friction coefficient (mu = 0.0 to 0.2, baseline 0.115), strain levels (up to 12%)
paper_records.dependent_variables: Axial stress-strain curves, reaction torque, contact normal and shear force distributions, energy dissipation
paper_records.model_used: Abaqus 3D solid element FEA with surface-to-surface penalty contact
paper_records.constitutive_model: Auricchio-Petrini 3D phenomenological superelastic constitutive model implemented in UMAT
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Penalty formulation Coulomb friction with isotropic friction coefficient mu = 0.115
paper_records.experiment_used: Validation against experimental data from Reedlunn et al. 2013
paper_records.experimental_setup: Exact 3D geometric CAD representation of wire ropes with helical sweeping and contact pair definitions
paper_records.key_results: Successfully reproduced the complete stress-strain response, transformation plateaus, work-hardening, and reaction torque of 1x27 and 7x7 NiTi cables using locked material parameters from single-wire tests; proved that inter-wire friction normal forces and relative slip directly modulate structural stiffness and energy dissipation.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that existing transformation-aware constitutive models coupled with standard Coulomb contact mechanics (H0b) are fully sufficient to predict multiwire NiTi bundle response.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not apply an active transverse fluid confinement pressure independent of axial tension.
directly_verified_statements: Abaqus FEA combining Auricchio UMAT with Coulomb friction (mu = 0.115) accurately predicts the complete cyclic response of 1x27 and 7x7 NiTi cables (Section 4, pp. 6-10).
Inter-wire friction increases axial stiffness and energy dissipation while reducing total recoverable strain (Section 4.3, pp. 11-13).
The model reproduces the experimental data of Reedlunn 2013 without introducing any new micro-coupling laws (Section 4.1, pp. 7-9).
inferred_statements: Unless an unpredicted phenomenon arises under transverse pressure, H0b is completely viable and live.
paper_records.limitations: Axial tension only; isothermal assumption; no transverse fluid pressure.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Decisive paper: closes C5/T1 at existence level and establishes H0b as a formidable, non-falsified competitor null hypothesis.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 4 (3D FEA mesh and contact definitions), Fig. 7 (validation against Reedlunn 1x27 and 7x7 data), Fig. 12 (friction sensitivity analysis)
paper_records.metadata_conflicts: Online first 2021, official journal issue published in 2022.

paper_records.paper_title: Nonlinear Vibration Isolation via a NiTiNOL Wire Rope
paper_records.repository_path: data/papers/verification/MP1-V002/A4-2021-Nonlinear vibration isolation via a nitinol wire rope.pdf
paper_records.matrix_filename: A4-2021-Nonlinear vibration isolation via a nitinol wire rope.pdf
paper_records.why_added: Demonstrates superelastic NiTi wire rope structures used as nonlinear variable-stiffness vibration isolators.
paper_records.threat_addressed: Threatens T1 and T3 by demonstrating that NiTi wire ropes provide tunable stiffness and damping under cyclic loading.
paper_records.method: Experimental vibration testing and nonlinear dynamic modeling
paper_records.loading_mode: Vertical dynamic base excitation and harmonic force excitation
paper_records.independent_variables: Vibration amplitude, excitation frequency across primary resonance
paper_records.dependent_variables: Transmissibility, resonant frequency shift, hysteretic loop area, dynamic stiffness
paper_records.model_used: Duffing-type nonlinear oscillator combined with hysteretic damping model
paper_records.constitutive_model: Polynomial restoring force combined with Bouc-Wen hysteresis
paper_records.contact_or_friction_model: Frictional dissipation represented via Bouc-Wen evolutionary variable
paper_records.experiment_used: Electrodynamic shaker, accelerometers, power amplifier, signal analyzer
paper_records.experimental_setup: NiTi wire rope isolator supporting a payload mass subjected to harmonic vertical vibration
paper_records.key_results: Demonstrated that NiTi wire ropes exhibit softening-hardening non-linear stiffness and high damping, reducing resonance peak transmissibility by up to 50% compared to steel wire rope isolators.
paper_records.what_it_proves: Proves that NiTi wire ropes modulate dynamic stiffness and dissipate energy under cyclic deformation.
paper_records.what_it_does_not_prove: Does not apply active pneumatic/hydraulic confinement pressure.
directly_verified_statements: NiTi wire rope isolators exhibit amplitude-dependent resonance frequency shifts due to superelastic softening (Section 3, pp. 6-9).
Superelasticity provides enhanced energy dissipation and displacement control over conventional steel wire ropes (Section 4, pp. 10-12).
inferred_statements: Variable stiffness in NiTi wire ropes is readily exploitable for dynamic stiffness tuning in soft systems.
paper_records.limitations: Lumped parameter dynamic testing; no local slip measurement.
paper_records.impact_on_MP1: Demonstrates prior art use of NiTi wire ropes for stiffness modulation.
paper_records.evidence_pointers: Fig. 5 (transmissibility curves), Fig. 8 (hysteresis loops under dynamic loading)
